chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain of transmission, saying: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said:

None of you should intercede in a hadd once it has reached the Imam, for he has no authority over it in that concerning which intercession is sought. But whatever has not reached the Imam, then its owner has authority over it, so intercede in what has not reached the Imam when you see remorse. And intercede in what has not reached the Imam, in matters other than the hadd, along with the return of the one interceded for, and do not intercede regarding the right of any Muslim, or anyone else, except with his permission.

key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the legitimate authority before whom the matter is brought
key_terms.الْمَشْفُوعِ لَهُ: the person on whose behalf intercession is made
key_terms.حَدٍّ: a prescribed legal punishment under sacred law
key_terms.حَقِّ: the due right or claim belonging to another person
key_terms.رُجُوعِ: returning from wrongdoing or turning back in repentance
key_terms.يَشْفَعَنَّ: to intercede or plead on behalf of someone

ai.seo_question: When is intercession allowed in hadd cases and other legal rights according to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets limits on intercession in judicial matters, distinguishing between cases that have already reached the Imam and those that have not. It teaches that prescribed legal punishments are not to be suspended through intercession once formally brought before legitimate authority, while intercession before that stage may be appropriate when remorse and repentance are evident, and when the rights of others are respected.
